sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-Hong Kong Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement
Luxembourg-Netherlands/Belgium Bilateral Treaties and Benelux Instruments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended including by the Law of 25 March 2020 implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 June 2019 relating to the functioning of the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 and subsequent CSSF AML/CFT circulars

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport (bio page) of each proposed shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National competent passport office in the UBO's home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille countries, full consular legalization of notarised copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised Power of Attorney (Pouvoir) executed by each shareholder in favour of the Luxembourg notary and incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the shareholder's country of domicile

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official corporate registry extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
Signed declaration countersigned by the home-country notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address or bank reference letter for each UBO and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal authority, utility provider, or licensed credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; recent bank reference letters may be accepted un-apostilled only with original bank stamp

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against PEP, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK HMT sanctions, and the Luxembourg national FIU watch list. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for politically exposed persons and high-risk third-country connections; screening must include parallel-naming algorithms to account for transliteration variance, documented false-positive resolution, and retained KYC audit trail for five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), online portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names are accepted in French, German, or Latin-alphabet transliteration; Luxembourgish may be used but is subject to RCS linguistic review. A non-Latin-script name must be accompanied by a statutory French/German transliteration. The name must include or be followed by the legal form 'société à responsabilité limitée' or the accepted abbreviation 'SARL', must be distinctive within the RCS to avoid confusion with existing or natural names, and must not be contrary to public order or good morals.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of a rejection notification, submit a reasoned objection to the LBR/RCS Registry; a final administrative appeal lies to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months, while urgent or irreparable prejudice may be brought before the President of the District Court by summary proceedings. All appeal filings must include the RCS rejection reference, legal grounds for reversal, and proposed corrected name; statutory representation fees are payable at the judicial tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted and agent-dependent. The SARL must have a statutory registered office in Luxembourg; pure virtual address arrangements are not compliant unless a licensed domiciliation agent actually receives mail and provides a physical administrative seat. For ISIC 8299 mail scanning and virtual office activity, use of a domiciliation address plus scanned-mail reception is acceptable only where the agent is authorized under the Law of 28 December 2017 and annual domiciliation declaration requirements are met.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% within the first twelve months if the entity operates only as a CMRA-style mail scanning service through a domiciliation agent; 50% where PEP or high-risk sanctions exposure triggers CSSF or FIU targeted administrative inspections. The registered office is subject to unannounced examination under the AML/CFT visitation powers of the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier and the RCS registrar.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and reservation application to RCS/LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under LBR/RCS fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary drafting, legal review, and execution of the SARL articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary in the district of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Grand-Ducal tariff for notarial acts; prevailing market range of EUR 1,100 to EUR 1,700

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle for up to five UBO/shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign ministries, competent apostille offices, and consular posts of the shareholders' home jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular and apostille fee schedules; average USD 50 to 75 per document plus courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO KYC/AML compliance package: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and Luxembourg sanctions screening with enhanced due diligence report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged corporate services provider or licensed AML compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced due diligence under Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Circular 20/735

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial domiciliation and virtual office mail scanning set-up fee for SARL registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate under Law of 28 December 2017 on domiciliation agents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration, statutory publication in the electronic register, UBO register filing, and administrative dues
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory filing fees set by the RCS/LBR regime

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Payment-routes pre-compliance assessment for Stripe Recurring and credit-card billing under PSD2 authentication requirements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Fintech compliance consultant or Luxembourg lawyer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for payment services and money-laundering risk mapping in a CMRA mail-scanning operating model

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 19 December 2016; Sàrl provisions under Articles 100–124; registration governed by the Law of 19 December 2016 on the Luxembourg Business Registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS/LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés), filed electronically with the RCS through the LBR/Guichet.lu portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an Sàrl is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid-up upon incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in an escrow account held by a Luxembourg notary or a Luxembourg credit institution and remain blocked until RCS registration. Contributions in kind require a certified auditor's report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers, having acceded to all articles of association, hereby ratify and confirm the subscription of the entire share capital of the company, as filed with the legal corporate records. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is established at the address stated in the articles within Luxembourg, which address shall serve as the company’s statutory seat and principal place of administration, to be used for lawful virtual-office and mail-scanning operations. FURTHER RESOLVED, that each appointed manager is duly confirmed and vested with full authority to represent the Sàrl and to execute all filings, and that the chairman and secretary are authorized to publish the incorporation and undertake all ancillary regulatory formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation company name clearance and notarial documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name reservation or negative certificate request through the LBR online portal or through a Luxembourg notary. Verify availability and absence of confusion with existing trade names. The notary then prepares the deed of incorporation and coordinated articles in French or German, ensuring the corporate object permits commercial mail receiving agency and digital scanning services.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or national ID and proof of residential address for each founder
Draft articles of association and proposed statutory object
Name reservation confirmation or negative certificate
Power of attorney executed by each founder if represented
AML/KYC identification form for each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or confusion, file a new name reservation and adjust the articles prior to notarization; the notary may resubmit within the same process without restarting the entire file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription and blocked escrow deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary's escrow account supervised by the Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked deposit account with a Luxembourg bank or use the notary's escrow. Transfer the minimum share capital amount of EUR 12,000 in cash, or provide an asset valuation report for any in-kind contribution. Obtain a bank certificate or notary attestation confirming receipt and blocking of funds.
required_dossiers: Capital subscription list signed by all subscribers
Bank transfer confirmation and blocked-funds certificate
Auditor's report on in-kind contribution, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML clarification, provide further source-of-wealth evidence or choose another Luxembourg credit institution; the escrow can be transferred to the notary's account without losing the subscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed and RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS, filed via the eJustice/LBR portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the Luxembourg notary in person or by proxy and execute the deed of incorporation and articles of association. The notary authenticates the capital certificate, accepts the appointment of managers, and submits the electronic filing package to the RCS. Upon successful registration, the company receives its RCS registration number and statutory extract.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate or notary attestation
Statements of acceptance by appointed managers
Details of registered office address and proof of availability of the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries or suspends the filing, the notary corrects the defects indicated and resubmits through the portal; any shortfall in documentary completeness is cured within the RCS-allocated legal window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic companies journal and post-formation confirmations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary or the company lodges the statutory publication of constitutional particulars in RESA. Verify that RCS extract correctly reflects legal form, registered office, managers and statutory object; then maintain updated corporate records and registers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles
Registered office confirmation, including lease or virtual-office agreement if compatible with Luxembourg law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or contains errors, contact LBR customer service to expedite publication; file a corrigendum through the RCS portal if any statutory datum must be corrected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Entrepreneurship (Direction des Classes Moyennes)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Authorization) for commercial services, including virtual-office and mail-receiving agency activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA – the ISIC 8299 mail-scanning/virtual-office activity is not listed in the mandatory EIA categories under the Luxembourg Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; only a general waste-handling registration is required if paper or electronic waste is managed on site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater and no significant VOC emission sources are generated by digital mail scanning; office wastewater must comply with municipal sewer regulations. Waste paper, toner cartridges and WEEE electronic waste must be separated and transferred to authorised waste operators under Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management and EU waste directives.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for the commercial premises; structural load attestation from the municipal building inspection; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) and affiliation with an approved external occupational health and safety service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD — Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified online portal MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu) for company registration, RCS incorporation, and tax ID activation; AEDT e-space (espace AEDT / MyGuichet) for VAT registration and filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A SARL is incorporated via a notary filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu, which automatically allocates (i) a national business registration number (numéro de matricule / RCS number L-prefix) used as the corporate tax TIN (NIF), and (ii) triggers a separate VAT identification number application to the AEDT. Non-resident foreign entities without a Luxembourg establishment obtain a Luxembourg direct-tax TIN upon first filing via the ACD and must apply for a VAT number (form 640 T.V.A., available via MyGuichet.lu / AEDT) before making taxable supplies in Luxembourg. No physical presence visit is required; e-desktop or authorized tax representative may complete the procedure. The VAT ID format is 'LU' followed by 8 digits (e.g., LU12345678).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) is an opaque corporation resident in Luxembourg; it is subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (communal trade tax / IAC), and net wealth tax on worldwide income/assets, with no statutory pass-through regime under Luxembourg domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' election exists under Luxembourg tax law; SARLs are per se corporate taxpayers. Available elective mechanisms: (1) VAT grouping (assujettissement collectif) election under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; (2) Luxembourg fiscal unity / tax consolidation election for direct taxes under Section 164 LIR (limited to resident corporate groups); (3) notional interest deduction (NID) election on equity increases; (4) IP box election (80% exemption for qualifying IP income under Article 50bis LIR); (5) hybrid mismatch self-assessment elections per ATAD implementing law (Law of 21 December 2018), including alignment of the SARL's tax classification with an EU/EEA parent's classification exclusively for hybrid mismatch avoidance; (6) for a single-member SARL, optional U.S. federal check-the-box classification (Form 8832) as disregarded or partnership is available for U.S. purposes because the SARL is not a per se corporation under U.S. Treasury Regulation §301.7701-2(b)(8), but this does not alter Luxembourg domestic tax opacity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi modifiée du 12 février 1979 concernant la TVA) implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for compulsory VAT registration of established taxable persons carrying out any economic activity; however, the small business exemption (Article 57 — régime de la franchise) applies to resident businesses with annual taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT) for goods and services (threshold raised from EUR 30,000 effective 1 January 2024). For non-resident suppliers, VAT registration in Luxembourg is required when taxable supplies are made in Luxembourg, subject to EU reverse-charge, distance-selling (EU EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold via OSS), and deemed-supplier rules; the EUR 128,000 Luxembourg intra-EU distance selling threshold applies to goods but is superseded by the Union OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API clearance regime for domestic B2B/B2C invoices in Luxembourg. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only in the B2G segment (suppliers to Luxembourg public authorities must submit PEPPOL / BIS Billing 3.0 format via the national e-invoicing platform (Espace e-Facturation) under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 2022). B2B electronic invoicing is voluntary and must comply with EU VAT invoicing rules (Articles 218–240 of the EU VAT Directive); e-invoices must guarantee authentic origin, content integrity, and legibility (e.g., EDI or XML with audit trail). Luxembourg is preparing for EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) requirements, with domestic B2B e-invoicing expected to be phased in from 2028 onward (agreement pending at EU level).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the seller or on its behalf to a destination outside the European Union (export under Article 155 of the EU VAT Directive / Articles 383–386 of the Luxembourg VAT Law), provided the goods physically leave EU territory within the statutory deadlines; and (ii) certain international services linked to immovable property abroad or, under the general B2B place-of-supply rule (Article 29 Luxembourg VAT Law), services supplied to a business customer established outside the EU, which are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT rather than zero-rated — including virtual office, mail scanning, and digital administrative services supplied to non-EU B2B clients. For the CMRA/mail-scanning activity, the core service is electronically supplied and will be out of scope of Luxembourg VAT if the recipient is a taxable person established in a non-EU country, or subject to reverse charge if established in another EU member state. Zero-rating for physical mail/parcel forwarding requires the export of goods evidenced by definitive export documents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (SAD / DAE) — Luxembourg customs export declaration (via LU-CLS / Descartes) with MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Commercial invoice and contract evidencing the service description and destination
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) with proof of physical departure from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank statement evidencing payment received from the foreign customer
Proof of identity and VAT status of the foreign recipient (VAT registration certificate or equivalent) for B2B place-of-supply substantiation
Audit trail of the digital service delivery (server logs, scan timestamps, mail forwarding receipts) for out-of-scope or zero-rated services
Transport documents and customs stamps for goods dispatched by the Luxembourg SARL to non-EU clients (when applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg customs and the AEDT conduct documented post-export checks (contrôles a posteriori) requiring proof of physical export and payment remittance within the statutory period; failure to substantiate zero-rating or out-of-scope treatment triggers immediate VAT reassessment at 17%, plus default interest (interest at the legal rate, currently 3.13% per annum for tax debts), and a negligence penalty of up to 10% of the tax due; fraudulent zero-rating claims (false customs declarations, fictitious exports, sham foreign establishments) constitute tax fraud (fraude fiscale) punishable by criminal fines up to EUR 250,000, imprisonment of up to 5 years, and retrospective clawback of VAT plus penalties for up to 10 years (statute of limitation; 10-year period applies in cases of fraud). The Luxembourg tax authority may also apply a 100% penalty for deliberate concealment and refer the matter to the Public Prosecutor's Office (Parquet) for prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and the Luxembourg Ministère des Finances, together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg applies full capital-account and current-account liberalisation under EU law (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 63-66) and OECD instruments. No exchange control authorisation is required for foreign direct investment, loan servicing, trade settlements or profit remittances. The only administrative requirements are statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the BCL for cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 and KYC/AML documentation substantiating the underlying economic purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion ratio applies. Luxembourg and the euro area do not require export proceeds to be converted into euro; exporters may retain receivables in any currency. Receipts must be declared for BCL balance-of-payments statistics, but no timeline or forced sale obligation exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Sprix / BCEE (Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, subject to strict legal conditions. A Luxembourg or other EEA-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Payment Institution passported into Luxembourg under PSD2 may provide account/IBAN and merchant acquiring services, but higher-risk virtual-office/CMRA business models trigger enhanced due diligence and possible account restrictions. Offshore, non-EEA digital EMIs are not viable for treasury-grade clearing because they lack SEPA/SWIFT direct membership, Luxembourg substance, and regulatory equivalence; use them only as a secondary collection rail, never for fiduciary escrows or tax-relevant flow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally require at least one managing director or beneficial owner with signing authority to attend an in-person or video-identification KYC interview. Remote opening is possible using a qualified electronic identification means accepted under eIDAS, but for an enhanced-risk CMRA/virtual-office SARL most Tier-1 banks will impose physical attendance of the compliance signatory, notarised corporate authorisations, apostilled (Convention de La Haye) identity documents, and proof of the Luxembourg registered office lease. If no resident director is present, banks may require a resident agent or add a 'high-risk client' rating with periodic reviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual office / mail scanning activity flagged as high-risk under Article 1 of the AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF guidance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full client onboarding policy for mail-scanning clients, the underlying client identification/verification records, AML/CFT risk assessment, physical registered-office lease contract, data-protection impact assessment, written service-level agreements, and evidence that the SARL does not act as a trust or company-service provider without the required licence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or opaque beneficial ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE) extract, group org chart, passport and proof of address for each natural-person UBO, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, tax identification numbers, and, where applicable, audited financial statements of the immediate parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate tax residence and Luxembourg substance risk (payer of last resort / treaty-shopping concerns)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Luxembourg articles of association, registered-office certificate, substance folder showing board meeting minutes held in Luxembourg, decision-making records, director mandates, employment or outsourced-service agreements with Luxembourg providers, utility bills, and the completed CSSF/BCL substance questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring credit-card and Stripe collections for mail/scanning fees without documentary proof of services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed merchant agreements, invoicing templates, evidence that card payments are tied to specific scanner-mailbox services, transaction-level pricing, reconciliation reports, refund policy, and any required registration as a payment facilitator or completion of Stripe's enhanced merchant risk review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear inbound equity payments / loans from foreign shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Arm the bank with the shareholders' resolution, share subscription ledger, share premium account documentation, signed loan agreements with market-rate interest, Central Balance Sheet Office filings, and BCL balance-of-payments reporting forms to demonstrate that inflows are legitimate equity or intercompany financing and not disguised crypto/third-party funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity must be sent via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own bank to the SARL's euro-denominated account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The wire reference must state 'share capital contribution' or 'equity subscription' and carry the appropriate BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment in a resident company (e.g. direct-investment equity/shares). The receiving bank will require board/shareholders' approval, the RBE extract, and proof of the Luxembourg notarised deed of incorporation/constitutive act before crediting the capital. Euro-area SEPA Credit Transfer may be used for payments within SEPA countries, but SWIFT MT103 is preferred for cross-continental clears and audit clarity; funds should not be commingled with turnover in the operational account if the capital is subject to escrow release conditions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for single cross-border payments to suppliers and service providers when supporting invoices exist; use SEPA Credit Transfer (XML ISO 20022 pain.001/pacs.003) for euro-denominated operational payments within SEPA; use a Documentary Letter of Credit (UCP 600) issued via a Luxembourg bank for material trade settlements to mitigate counterparty risk and ensure transport-document compliance. For recurring service revenues from credit-card/Stripe rails, settle only onto the merchant account and sweep the net balance daily/weekly to the Tier-1 operating account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts (matching committed cash flows)
FX swaps (buy/sell euro against another currency with agreed reversal date)
Cross-currency swaps (fixed/floating CCS) for financing and intercompany loan exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with non-convertible or restricted onshore markets, only where cash settlement in euro is permissible and governed by an ISDA/CSA
Standard vanilla FX options (call/put) purchased for risk protection, subject to BCL statistical reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) of the SARL: balance sheet, profit and loss account, annex, and shareholders' approval evidence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end (shareholder approval within 6 months; RCS deposit within 1 month after approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger administrative penalties up to EUR 500; continued non-compliance after court order can lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) of the SARL and loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation in the RBE (beneficiaires effectifs) and any required update following shareholding transfers or UBO changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once each calendar year; for shareholding transfers or UBO changes, filing within one month of the change or of the company becoming aware of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation or late UBO update is sanctioned by administrative fines generally between EUR 500 and EUR 5,000, with higher criminal penalties in case of willful omission; persistent default may be escalated to RCS strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg corporate income tax return (CIT) and net wealth tax return (NWT) for the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year N, filing due no later than 31 December of year N+1 (calendar-year taxpayers); extensions may be granted on request by the ACD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an automatic increase (usually 10%) of the assessed CIT/NWT plus late-payment interest at the statutory monthly rate; willful failure may lead to forced tax assessment and criminal fines against managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg VAT return (form 106) if the SARL is subject to annual VAT filing regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 1 May of the following calendar year for VAT periods ending on 31 December (unless monthly/quarterly regime applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment may attract a 10% late-payment increase, monthly default interest on VAT due, and administrative fines; continued failure allows forced assessment and recovery through tax execution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is mandatory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds at balance sheet date: total assets EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average staff 50. Mandatory audit also applies to public-interest entities, credit/financial undertakings, and any SARL whose articles so require.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 10 August 1915 and the modified Law of 19 December 2019 on annual and consolidated accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted/required for consolidated or listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once per calendar year the SARL must confirm through the RBE online portal that the beneficial ownership data remain accurate. Each shareholding transfer or change of entitlement must additionally be filed with the RBE within one month; the annual confirmation remains due even if the data are unchanged. The RBE declaration must clearly identify the natural persons ultimately owning or controlling the SARL and must remain consistent with the RCS registered office and the virtual office mail scanning business scope.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 - 4,400 per annum for a Luxembourg registered office / corporate agent with mail scanning and forwarding service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 per annum for a moderate-sized SARL requiring a certified statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Aggregate headline rate of 24.94% for a Luxembourg SARL tax-resident with management seat in Luxembourg City = national corporate income tax (CIT/IRC) of 17% + solidarity surcharge of 7% on CIT (1.19%) + municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC) of 6.75% (Luxembourg City communal multiplier 225%; commune range 6.00%–12.50%). The ICC is deductible in computing the national CIT base, producing an effective aggregate rate of approximately 24.94% pre-deduction and roughly 24.66% after the ICC deduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (Art. 166 LIR): 100% exclusion from the taxable base of qualifying dividend income and realized capital gains where the SARL holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's share capital or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million, with a 12-month holding period and a subject-to-tax condition. Innovation box: 80% exemption of qualifying net intellectual-property income, yielding an effective CIT rate of approximately 4.5%–5% (not applicable to mail-scanning services unless embedded software/IP qualifies). Net wealth tax (IFT) at 0.5% of taxable net wealth with minimum tax bands of approximately EUR 535 / EUR 1,605 / EUR 4,815 depending on balance-sheet totals. No preferential regime applies to standalone low-margin services; virtual-office and mail-scanning fee income is fully taxable on an arm's-length net margin.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited – no statutory time limit (perte reportable without expiry under Art. 114 LIR); no carryback. The offset of carried-forward losses is restricted to income from the same commercial business activity, and the loss carryforward is forfeited upon a change of business activity, cessation of the undertaking, or a controlling-ownership change combined with abandonment of the loss-generating activity.
